In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Hudson River was the major source for the outer margin off the mid- Atlantic states, but that other fluvial sources, especially the Delaware and Susquehanna Rivers, were also important.
, in contrast to other sectors of the continental margin, the outer continental margin of the mid-Atlantic States is characterized by a relatively uniform mineral assemblage.
the mineralogic character of the outer margin sand off the mid- Atlantic states reflects the combined effects of a large glaciated region to the north and a large drainage system to the west.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the mineralogic composition and the inferred provenance of the sand-size sediment on the outer margin off the mid- Atlantic States are largely the product of a major drainage system that has migrated extensively across the shelf and slope.

the mineralogic composition and vertical time-related variability of sand-sized sediment on the outer margin of the middle Atlantic Bight is largely a function of the influence of the ancestral Hudson and other major fluvial systems draining the glaciated Appalachian Plateau and Piedmont regions.

, although the mineralogic data do not permit a precise definition of the ancestral Hudson's southern limit, the evidence does suggest that it was probably much farther south than the previously postulated 40 km south of the head of Baltimore or Norfolk Canyons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mineralogic composition is not a good indicator for the source of the sand.
it is not possible, on the basis of mineralogy alone, to identify specific drainage areas as sources for sand-size sediment on the outer shelf and slope of the mid-Atlantic margin.

, although the ancestral Hudson River probably had the greatest influence on the mineralogic composition and distribution of sand on the outer continental margin off the mid- Atlantic states, it is not the sole or even the most dominant source of sand.
